samples.summary: New user-facing login error banner (`?error=login_state` → mapped message, plus fallback) has no test at all
samples.evidence: login-form.tsx now reads `useSearchParams()` and renders a `role="alert"` div using ERROR_MESSAGES[error] ?? FALLBACK_ERROR. This is the only feedback a user gets when the OAuth callback refuses their login (the backend redirects to `/login?error=login_state`). Frontend has a running vitest lane with many component tests (e.g. packages/frontend/src/components/__tests__/datasource-dialog.test.tsx, app/files/__tests__/generic-file-view.test.tsx), but there is no test file for login-form or the login page — a regression that dropped the banner or the fallback mapping would ship silently.

samples.summary: The `sawUnboundCode` timeout message branch is never exercised — the only timeout test asserts the generic /timed out/ message
samples.evidence: startCallbackServer records `sawUnboundCode = true` when a callback arrives with `state === null`, and the timeout rejection then produces a different, longer message ('Login callback carried no `state`…'). packages/cli/test/login-callback.test.ts only tests (a) a state-less callback returning 400 and (b) a timeout with no callback at all asserting `rejects.toThrow(/timed out/i)`. No test drives a state-less callback and then advances to the timeout, so the diagnostic branch — the whole reason the flag exists — could be inverted or dropped with the suite still green.

samples.summary: `failFromBackend`'s exit-1 (HTTP_ERROR) branch is untested; only the 401→exit 2 and 5xx→exit 2 rows are covered
samples.evidence: `codeForStatus` maps 401/403→UNAUTHORIZED, >=500→SYSTEM, everything else→HTTP_ERROR, and the exit code branches on that (`process.exit(code === 'HTTP_ERROR' ? 1 : 2)`). packages/cli/test/login-callback.test.ts adds tests for a 401 exchange (exit 2) and a 502 workspaces call (exit 2), but no test for a 4xx-other status, so the HTTP_ERROR code and its distinct exit code are asserted nowhere.

samples.summary: `announceLoginUrl`'s TTY branch and its failure fallback are untested — only the non-TTY file branch is covered
samples.evidence: announceLoginUrl has three outcomes: print the URL when `process.stderr.isTTY`, write it to a 0600 file otherwise, or print the 'could not open a browser' guidance when the write throws. The login test only runs under a non-TTY vitest stderr, asserting the file path is announced and the file is removed afterwards. Nothing asserts that on a TTY the URL is printed (nor that it is NOT written to disk), and nothing exercises the write-failure fallback.

samples.summary: The controller's own CLI port range check (`port < 1024 || port > 65535` → BadRequestException) has no test
samples.evidence: auth.controller.spec.ts's `startCliLogin` helper always uses port 9876 (or an override that no test supplies out of range), so the controller-side range guard at auth.controller.ts:254-257 is never reached. The equivalent guard-side check is tested in github-auth.guard.spec.ts ('refuses a CLI start whose port is missing or out of range'), but that is a different code path — deleting the controller check would leave every test green.
searchedFor: read auth.controller.spec.ts CLI describe in diff

samples.summary: `issueLoginCookie`'s InternalServerErrorException path (no `res.cookie` on the response) is untested
samples.evidence: The guard deliberately throws InternalServerErrorException('Cannot start a login session') when the response object cannot set cookies, on the reasoning that a silently-unset binding would look like a CSRF hit at the callback. github-auth.guard.spec.ts's `contextFor` always supplies a response with `cookie` and `clearCookie`, so no test constructs a context without them; the guard rail could be removed without any test failing.
searchedFor: grep 'Cannot start a login session' in packages/backend/src
read github-auth.guard.spec.ts contextFor helper in diff

samples.summary: `escapeHtml` on the consent page is only exercised for `&`; no test renders a nonce or path containing HTML metacharacters
samples.evidence: The consent-page tests use nonce 'n0nce-x/y', port 9876 and path '/auth/github', so the only escape actually observed is `&` → `&` (asserted via `expect(html).toContain('/auth/github?mode=cli&port=9876')`). The nonce is validated by `boundedToken(req.query?.nonce, 1, MAX_NONCE_LENGTH)` with no character pattern (unlike code_challenge), so it can contain `"`, `<`, `'`. Nothing asserts the rendered markup stays safe for such a value — if escapeHtml or the URLSearchParams encoding were changed, no test would notice.
searchedFor: read 'GET /auth/github — CLI consent page' describe in diff

samples.summary: No test spans guard → controller for the CLI flow: the controller spec mints state directly through CliAuthStore, so a guard/controller mismatch in cookie naming or binding would pass
samples.evidence: `startCliLogin` calls `cliAuthStore.createState({...})` and hand-builds `cookies: { wafflebase_cli_state: browserBinding }` rather than driving GitHubAuthGuard.canActivate and feeding the cookie it actually set into the callback. The web flow is partly protected against drift because it recomputes the state via the shared `stateSignature(bindingSecret(...))`, but the CLI cookie name is hard-coded as the bare `wafflebase_cli_state` while the production path uses `loginCookieName()` (`__Host-` prefixed). A divergence between what the guard writes and what the callback reads would not be caught by either spec.

samples.summary: No test asserts the pino `req` serializer actually routes through `logSafeUrl`
samples.evidence: log-safe-url.spec.ts covers the helper thoroughly, but the wiring in app.module.ts (`url: logSafeUrl(req.url)`) is only asserted by the diff itself. Reverting that one line to `req.url` would leave the entire new spec green while restoring the credential-in-logs behavior the change exists to prevent.

finding.summary: New user-facing login error banner (`?error=login_state` → mapped message, plus fallback) has no test at all

This is the only feedback a user gets when the OAuth callback refuses their login (the backend redirects to `/login?error=login_state`). Frontend has a running vitest lane with many component tests (e.g. packages/frontend/src/components/__tests__/datasource-dialog.test.tsx, app/files/__tests__/generic-file-view.test.tsx), but there is no test file for login-form or the login page — a regression that dropped the banner or the fallback mapping would ship silently.

verdict.reason: The claimed behavior is real and untested. login-form.tsx:27-50 reads useSearchParams(), and when `error` is present renders a role="alert" div with `ERROR_MESSAGES[error] ?? FALLBACK_ERROR` (login_state → "That sign-in link expired…", else the fallback). I searched the whole frontend test surface — colocated `src/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}`, the separate `packages/frontend/tests/**` suite, every `__tests__` directory, and any e2e/playwright/cypress layer (none exists) — and grepped for the banner's literal strings, for `role="alert"` in tests, and for router-based renders (MemoryRouter appears in only 4 tests, none touching login). No test file for login-form or the login page exists anywhere in the repo; the only `*login*` test is packages/cli/test/login-callback.test.ts, which covers the CLI loopback callback, not this component. The nearest coverage is backend-side (auth.controller.spec.ts:540,557,572) asserting the redirect to `/login?error=login_state` — that tests the producer of the query param and would stay green if the banner, the login_state mapping, or the fallback branch were deleted. A new user-facing behavior with no meaningful test at all is major under the test-adequacy rubric.
